title: LockBit, 2.0 → 3.0
deck: LockBit’s paper trail: the 2022 FBI flash, the 2023 CISA advisories, and a 2026 vendor snapshot. Historical reporting, mapped to ATT&CK v20.0.
scope: The main case is historical LockBit reporting from February 2022 to June 2023, mapped to ATT&CK v20.0. The 2026 LockBit 5.0 snapshot is vendor reporting and sits outside the diff counts.
universeNote: The diff only uses the 26 and 34 techniques ATT&CK v20.0 maps to LockBit 2.0 and 3.0. Advisory-only techniques do not count. The 2026 vendor snapshot stays separate.

snapshots.label: LockBit 2.0
snapshots.period: Observed since at least June 2021 · snapshot 4 Feb 2022
snapshots.summary: The FBI flash describes a heavily obfuscated Windows encryptor, GPO-driven domain encryption, Stealbit exfiltration and a language exclusion check.
snapshots.limitations: The FBI flash is an IOC bulletin, not an exhaustive TTP catalogue. Some ATT&CK mappings come from vendor analysis cited by MITRE.

snapshots.label: LockBit 3.0
snapshots.period: Observed since at least June 2022 · snapshot 14 Jun 2023
snapshots.summary: The 2023 advisories document a more modular build: password-gated payloads, Safe Mode reboot, mutex checks, PsExec spreading and broader defence impairment.
snapshots.limitations: The June advisory covers LockBit affiliates broadly, not just 3.0. The March advisory is the stronger source for build-specific behaviour.

snapshots.label: LockBit 5.0 (2026 vendor)
snapshots.summary: Acronis and AhnLab describe a multi-platform 5.0 build with packing, process hollowing, ETW patching, log clearing and faster encryption. Check Point and Bitdefender track the 2025–2026 victim comeback.
snapshots.limitations: Vendor research, not an official advisory or a complete ATT&CK mapping. The 2026 activity is separate from the 2022–2023 historical diff.

caveats: The main diff is historical: Feb 2022 – Jun 2023. ATT&CK v20.0 is the map we use today, not a claim about 2026 activity.
The 2026 snapshot is vendor research, not an official advisory. It does not re-document the whole intrusion chain.
A new line in a later report can mean better reporting, not new behaviour.
A missing rule here only means it is missing from this catalogue, not from your detection stack.
These counts are about documentation. They are not incident frequency.

currentReporting.headline: LockBit 5.0, as vendors saw it
currentReporting.deck: LockBit came back in 2025 and kept showing up in 2026. Acronis and AhnLab pulled apart the 5.0 build; Check Point and Bitdefender tracked the victims. This is vendor reporting, not an official advisory.
currentReporting.caveat: Vendor research only. It is a build analysis plus activity context, not a full ATT&CK mapping. Keep it separate from the 2022–2023 diff.
